arxiv-2110-05697.title: Hierarchical Modeling for Task Recognition and Action Segmentation in Weakly-Labeled Instructional Videos
arxiv-2110-05697.creator: Reza Ghoddoosian Saif Sayed Vassilis Athitsos
arxiv-2110-05697.description: Abstract This paper 1 1 1 https://github.com/rezaghoddoosian/Hierarchical-Task-Modeling focuses on task recognition and action segmentation in weakly-labeled instructional videos, where only the ordered sequence of video-level actions is available during training. We propose a two-stream framework, which exploits semantic and temporal hierarchies to recognize top-level tasks in instructional videos.

arxiv-2111-01595.title: Scattering and absorption of a scalar field impinging on a charged black hole in the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory
arxiv-2111-01595.creator: Martín G. Richarte, Ébano L. Martins, Júlio C. Fabris
arxiv-2111-01595.description: Abstract This study revisits the absorption and scattering process by which a massless scalar field impinges on a charged dilatonic black hole. First, we review the classical analysis to obtain the deflection angle and the differential scattering cross-section in terms of the mass, electric charge and dilatonic charge.

arxiv-2308-01281.title: Boundary conditions and infrared divergences Journal: …
arxiv-2308-01281.creator: Lissa de Souza Campos †⋆, Claudio Dappiaggi †⋆, Luca Sinibaldi †⋆
arxiv-2308-01281.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lissa de Souza Campos †⋆, Claudio Dappiaggi †⋆, Luca Sinibaldi †⋆. We review the procedure to construct quasi-free ground states, for real scalar fields whose dynamics is dictated by the Klein-Gordon equation, on standard static Lorentzian manifolds with a time-like boundary.

arxiv-2310-05246.title: Formulations and Constructions of Remote State Preparation with Verifiability, with Applications
arxiv-2310-05246.creator: Jiayu Zhang
arxiv-2310-05246.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jiayu Zhang. Remote state preparation with verifiability (RSPV) is an important quantum cryptographic primitive [ 27 , 53 ] . In this primitive, a client would like to prepare a quantum state (sampled or chosen from a state family) on the server side, such that ideally the client knows its full description, while the server holds and only holds the state itself. In this work we make several contributions on its formulations, constructions and applications.

arxiv-2503-14109.title: Operational Change Detection for Geographical Information: Overview and Challenges
arxiv-2503-14109.creator: Nicolas Gonthier
arxiv-2503-14109.description: Abstract The rapid evolution of territories due to climate change and human impact necessitates prompt and effective updates to geospatial databases maintained by National Mapping Agencies. That is why change detection is a rapidly evolving and increasingly important field with crucial applications in environmental monitoring, urban expansion, and disaster management.

arxiv-2506-08004.title: Dynamic View Synthesis as an Inverse Problem
arxiv-2506-08004.creator: Hidir Yesiltepe, Pinar Yanardag, pinary@vt.edu
arxiv-2506-08004.description: Abstract In this work, we address dynamic view synthesis from monocular videos as an inverse problem in a training-free setting. By redesigning the noise initialization phase of a pre-trained video diffusion model, we enable high-fidelity dynamic view synthesis without any weight updates or auxiliary modules.

arxiv-2506-09696.creator: Joseph Corneli, Charles J. Danoff, Raymond S. Puzio, Sridevi Ayloo, Serge Belich, Mary Tedeschi
arxiv-2506-09696.description: Abstract . Building on earlier installments, this paper re-examines the PLACARD pattern. We report on a series of workshops where PLACARD was used to scaffold collaborative reflection, speculative inquiry, and stimulate design pattern generation. These accounts are enriched by a comparison case: virtual workshops carried out with simple AI-based chatbots.

arxiv-2510-01248.title: SSTAG: Structure-Aware Self-Supervised Learning Method for Text-Attributed Graphs
arxiv-2510-01248.creator: Ruyue Liu, Rong Yin, Xiangzhen Bo, Xiaoshuai Hao, Yong Liu, Jinwen Zhong, Can Ma, Weiping Wang
arxiv-2510-01248.description: Abstract Large-scale pre-trained models have revolutionized Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Computer Vision (CV), showcasing remarkable cross-domain generalization abilities. However, in graph learning, models are typically trained on individual graph datasets, limiting their capacity to transfer knowledge across different graphs and tasks.

arxiv-2602-17120.title: HybridPrompt: Bridging Generative Priors and Traditional Codecs for Mobile Streaming Conference: Workshop on Network and Operating System Support for Digital Audio and Video; April 4–8, 2026; Hong Kong, Hong Kong Workshop on Network and Operating System Support for Digital Audio and Video (NOSSDAV ’
arxiv-2602-17120.creator: Liming Liu, Jiangkai Wu, Haoyang Wang, Peiheng Wang, Zongming Guo, Xinggong Zhang
arxiv-2602-17120.description: Abstract . In Video on Demand (VoD) scenarios, traditional codecs are the industry standard due to their high decoding efficiency. However, they suffer from severe quality degradation under low bandwidth conditions. While emerging generative neural codecs offer significantly higher perceptual quality, their reliance on heavy frame-by-frame generation makes real-time playback on mobile devices impractical.

arxiv-2602-18899.title: [b] = = [d] − - [t] + + [p]: Self-supervised Speech Models Discover Phonological Vector Arithmetic
arxiv-2602-18899.creator: Kwanghee Choi, Eunjung Yeo, Cheol Jun Cho, David Harwath, David R. Mortensen
arxiv-2602-18899.description: Abstract Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) are known to encode rich phonetic information, yet how this information is structured remains underexplored. We conduct a comprehensive study across 96 languages to analyze the underlying structure of S3M representations, with particular attention to phonological vectors. We first show that there exist linear directions within the model’s representation space that correspond to phonological features.

pmc-10650736.title: Silver Bionanocomposites as Active Food Packaging: Recent Advances & Future Trends Tackling the Food Waste Crisis
pmc-10650736.creator: Federico Trotta, Sidonio Da Silva, Alessio Massironi, Seyedeh Fatemeh Mirpoor, Stella Lignou, Sameer Khalil Ghawi, Dimitris Charalampopoulos
pmc-10650736.description: Food waste is a pressing global challenge leading to over $1 trillion lost annually and contributing up to 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Extensive study has been directed toward the use of active biodegradable packaging materials to improve food quality, minimize plastic use, and encourage sustainable packaging technology development.

pmc-11491686.title: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) in a patient with post streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN): A case report
pmc-11491686.creator: Aftab Ahmed, Anum Akbar, Digbijay Kunwar, Fena Mehta
pmc-11491686.description: Key Clinical MessageConcurrent recurrence of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) and poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN) in a thalassemia intermedia patient is rare and underscores the complexity of autoimmune disorders. This case emphasizes the importance of considering ADEM in the differential diagnosis of children presenting with PSGN accompanied by neurological symptoms.AbstractPost‐streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN) is a common group A streptococcal (GAS) infection sequela.

pmc-11641955.title: Endothelial Glycocalyx Anomalies and Ocular Manifestations in Patients with Post-Acute COVID-19
pmc-11641955.creator: Georges Azar, Youssef Abdelmassih, Sophie Bonnin, Damien Guindolet, Vivien Vasseur, Francine Behar Cohen, Dominique Salmon, Martine Mauget-Faÿsse, Brent Siesky
pmc-11641955.description: Objectives: To report ophthalmological and microvascular findings in patients with post-acute COVID-19. Methods: In this prospective, monocentric cohort study, we included patients with post-acute COVID-19 who presented with ophthalmological symptoms. All patients underwent indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), OCT, OCT-angiography, adaptive optics, and GlycoCheck assessments. Results: We included 44 patients, predominantly female (81.8%), with a mean age of 47.5 ± 11.

pmc-12423943.title: Preoperative Factors Associated With Falls Following Total Hip Arthroplasty in Older Adults
pmc-12423943.creator: Craig P Hensley, Abel N Kho, Andrew Kritselis, Jing Song, Jungwha Lee, Alison H Chang
pmc-12423943.description: ObjectiveFalls are common after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and can cause serious complications. Understanding preoperative factors linked to falls post‐THA can inform discharge planning and management to lower fall risk. We aimed to identify preoperative factors associated with falls occurring within one year following THA in older adults.MethodsWe performed a retrospective cohort study using records within a large hospital system.

pmc-12572133.title: Pitfalls in using ML to predict cognitive function performance
pmc-12572133.creator: Gianna Kuhles, Sami Hamdan, Stefan Heim, Simon B Eickhoff, Kaustubh R Patil, Julia A Camilleri, Susanne Weis
pmc-12572133.description: Machine learning analyses are widely used for predicting cognitive abilities, yet there are pitfalls that need to be considered during their implementation and interpretation of the results. Hence, the present study aimed at drawing attention to the risks of erroneous conclusions incurred by confounding variables illustrated by a case example predicting executive function (EF) performance by prosodic features.

pmc-12577219.title: Attitude of consumers towards community pharmacy services in Oman: a qualitative approach
pmc-12577219.creator: Hisham Amjad Abdul Razzaq, Amer Hayat Khan, Syed Azhar Syed Sulaiman, Sabin Thomas
pmc-12577219.description: BackgroundConsumers are the main hub of the healthcare system, and assessing their perceptions towards the healthcare services is a paramount indicator that helps policymakers shape and develop healthcare services to meet their needs.AimThis study aims to explore consumer perceptions and identify suggestions for improving community pharmacy services (CPS) in Oman.

pmc-13066633.title: Continuous observation of Parkinsonian symptoms using symptom diaries & wearable accelerometry
pmc-13066633.creator: T. P. R. Nesser, C. van der Linden, C. Schedlich-Teufer, G. Brandt, M. T. Barbe, T. A. Dembek
pmc-13066633.description: Treatment adjustments in Parkinson’s Disease (PD) are often based on clinical evaluations at single time points which are insufficient to adequately assess real-life motor fluctuations. Patient-written symptom diaries on the other hand are highly subjective and require well-educated and adherent patients to provide reliable results.

pmc-13071291.title: Somatosensory evoked potential monitoring for position-related brachial plexus injury during cerebellopontine angle tumor resection: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-13071291.creator: Xian Jiang, Yanyi Yin, Xiaomin Hou, Jun Liu, Peng Li
pmc-13071291.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the utility of intraoperative somatosensory evoked potential monitoring for detecting position-related brachial plexus injury during cerebellopontine angle tumor resection, identify independent risk factors, and assess the effectiveness of somatosensory evoked potential–guided interventions.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 45 patients who underwent cerebellopontine angle microsurgery in the lateral or semilateral position. Median nerve somatosensory evoked potentials were continuously monitored.

pmc-13396064.title: Real-World Treatment Switch Rates, and Healthcare Costs of Botulinum Toxin Type A Among Patients with Cervical Dystonia in the USA: A Retrospective Claims Analysis
pmc-13396064.creator: Ning Cheng, Annaliza Dominguez, Shivaji R. Manthena, Darshini Shah
pmc-13396064.description: IntroductionReal-world evidence on comparative treatment patterns and cost is limited for botulinum toxin type A (BoNTA) treatments for cervical dystonia (CD). This study aims to evaluate treatment switch rates, healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), and healthcare costs among patients with cervical dystonia initiating BoNTAs in the USA.

pmc-13520126.title: Evidence of biological nitrification inhibition in barley to support sustainable nitrogen management
pmc-13520126.creator: Jack Henderson, Xiaoping Fan, Ellen Elizabeth Smith, Marcel Jaspars, Timothy S George, Cécile Gubry-Rangin
pmc-13520126.description: Nitrification drives nitrogen loss in agricultural systems, resulting in leached nitrate and increased emissions of the greenhouse gas nitrous oxide, thereby reducing nitrogen use efficiency (NUE). Biological nitrification inhibition (BNI) provides a promising nature-based solution to low-NUE by suppressing nitrifying microorganisms via plant-exuded bioactive metabolites.

pmc-13680590.title: Organization of the first national workshop for families in Switzerland concerned with hereditary cancer syndromes
pmc-13680590.creator: Sarah Glick, Monica Aceti, Claire M Barton, Bettina M Zimmermann, Lisa Schiess, Muriel Fluri, Andrea Kaiser-Grolimund, Carla Pedrazzani, Elissa Azzi, Arianna Maria Elena Bonfanti, Barbara Peters, Benjamin Thiele, Pierre O Chappuis, Maria Caiata-Zufferey, Maria C Katapodi, The CASCADE Consortium
pmc-13680590.description: BackgroundAlthough Patient and Public Involvement (PPI) workshops with families affected by hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes can benefit both affected individuals and their support networks, PPI workshops are rarely being organized. This article presents the planning and implementation of a one-day PPI workshop for families affected by Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer (HBOC) or Lynch Syndrome (LS) in Switzerland.
